newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - GIST-BROCADES H1 PROFIT TO RISE.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - GIST-BROCADES H1 PROFIT TO RISE.

text.p: Dutch biochemicals and food group Gist-Brocades NV is expected to report a rise of about 15 percent in first half profit despite downward pressure on antibiotic prices, analysts said on Monday.
Forecasts of profit, to be issued on Thursday, range from 72 million to 76 million guilders, compared with a net profit of 64.4 million guilders in the first half of 1995.

Gist's bakery ingredients division is expected to show improvements as the yeast market in Europe emerges from a trough, said analysts, adding that the dollar's rise against the guilder should also have enhanced profits.
"The dollar has been somewhat stronger in the second quarter and that will prove positive for Gist," said Peter Beijers, an analyst at Kempen and Company.
Divestment over the past year of activities, including enzymes for detergents and U.S. yeast, had also strengthened the company, Beijers said.
However, analysts are not quite so confident about the performance of and prospects for Gist's antibiotics business.
"We're a bit more cautious about the pharmaceutical areas," said Andreas de Groot, chemicals analyst at Mees Pierson.

A harsh winter, which slowed bacteria reproduction, has led to fewer colds and sickness and a smaller market for medicines. Chinese production has grown, putting additional pressure on antibiotics prices.
"The price went down because of oversupply from China and there's no way to create demand if people are not ill," said Quirijn Mulder at ING Baring Research.
Analysts believe Gist will not suffer as much as other companies in the industry as most of Gist's production does not enter the spot market.
Cost savings, such as joint production with SmithKline Beecham in Scotland, volume growth in the western hemisphere and superior products should help Gist weather the storm, analysts say.
However, analysts will watch projected earnings in the second half when the effect of pharmaceutical price falls may filter through to the company.
"The outlook for the second half - that's going to move the stock," said de Groot.
